title: CPR in microgravity (weightless only; see coverage.json for each environment)

steps.text: Start CPR in a crewmember who appears to be in cardiac arrest, even if no defibrillator is available.

source.guideline: Hinkelbein J, et al. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) during spaceflight - a guideline for CPR in microgravity from the German Society of Aerospace Medicine (DGLRM) and the European Society of Aerospace Medicine Space Medicine Group (ESAM-SMG). Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med. 2020;28:108. doi:10.1186/s13049-020-00793-y

steps.text: For initial Basic Life Support at the site of the emergency, apply the Evetts-Russomano (ER) method first. If you cannot give adequate chest compressions with ER, switch to the Reverse-Bear-Hug (RBH) method.

source.guideline: Hinkelbein J, et al. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) during spaceflight - a guideline for CPR in microgravity from the German Society of Aerospace Medicine (DGLRM) and the European Society of Aerospace Medicine Space Medicine Group (ESAM-SMG). Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med. 2020;28:108. doi:10.1186/s13049-020-00793-y
source.section: Results and recommendations, Recommendation 2 (one rescuer, no restraint, no equipment: rationale for Recommendation 1)

steps.text: As soon as the patient is restrained on the Crew Medical Restraint System, give chest compressions with the Handstand method (HS), if the spacecraft dimensions and the rescuer's height allow it.

source.guideline: Hinkelbein J, et al. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) during spaceflight - a guideline for CPR in microgravity from the German Society of Aerospace Medicine (DGLRM) and the European Society of Aerospace Medicine Space Medicine Group (ESAM-SMG). Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med. 2020;28:108. doi:10.1186/s13049-020-00793-y

steps.text: If the HS method seems impossible, use restrained CPR in the standard or the straddling position.

source.guideline: Hinkelbein J, et al. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) during spaceflight - a guideline for CPR in microgravity from the German Society of Aerospace Medicine (DGLRM) and the European Society of Aerospace Medicine Space Medicine Group (ESAM-SMG). Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med. 2020;28:108. doi:10.1186/s13049-020-00793-y

steps.text: An automated chest compression device could be used on a restrained patient, if available. Installing it should not delay high-quality chest compressions.

source.guideline: Hinkelbein J, et al. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) during spaceflight - a guideline for CPR in microgravity from the German Society of Aerospace Medicine (DGLRM) and the European Society of Aerospace Medicine Space Medicine Group (ESAM-SMG). Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med. 2020;28:108. doi:10.1186/s13049-020-00793-y

steps.text: Use the AED only when the patient is restrained to an electrically isolated, safe surface such as the Crew Medical Restraint System. Use self-adhesive defibrillation pads.

source.guideline: Hinkelbein J, et al. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) during spaceflight - a guideline for CPR in microgravity from the German Society of Aerospace Medicine (DGLRM) and the European Society of Aerospace Medicine Space Medicine Group (ESAM-SMG). Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med. 2020;28:108. doi:10.1186/s13049-020-00793-y

steps.text: Defibrillation should take place when appropriate, even if survival is likely to be reduced.

source.guideline: Hinkelbein J, et al. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) during spaceflight - a guideline for CPR in microgravity from the German Society of Aerospace Medicine (DGLRM) and the European Society of Aerospace Medicine Space Medicine Group (ESAM-SMG). Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med. 2020;28:108. doi:10.1186/s13049-020-00793-y

steps.text: Manage the airway only if at least two rescuers are present and the patient has been restrained.

source.guideline: Hinkelbein J, et al. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) during spaceflight - a guideline for CPR in microgravity from the German Society of Aerospace Medicine (DGLRM) and the European Society of Aerospace Medicine Space Medicine Group (ESAM-SMG). Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med. 2020;28:108. doi:10.1186/s13049-020-00793-y

steps.text: If no rescuer with extensive training in tracheal intubation is present, use a second-generation supraglottic airway device for airway management. Keep a manual suction device ready.

source.guideline: Hinkelbein J, et al. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) during spaceflight - a guideline for CPR in microgravity from the German Society of Aerospace Medicine (DGLRM) and the European Society of Aerospace Medicine Space Medicine Group (ESAM-SMG). Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med. 2020;28:108. doi:10.1186/s13049-020-00793-y

steps.text: Tracheal intubation remains the gold standard if a skilled provider performs it. Restrain patient and rescuer on the Crew Medical Restraint System during the attempt. Keep a manual suction device ready.

source.guideline: Hinkelbein J, et al. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) during spaceflight - a guideline for CPR in microgravity from the German Society of Aerospace Medicine (DGLRM) and the European Society of Aerospace Medicine Space Medicine Group (ESAM-SMG). Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med. 2020;28:108. doi:10.1186/s13049-020-00793-y

steps.text: Attempt venous access only if more than two rescuers are present and high-quality CPR is being performed. Use a peripheral vein first; if that fails, use the intraosseous tibial route.

source.guideline: Hinkelbein J, et al. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) during spaceflight - a guideline for CPR in microgravity from the German Society of Aerospace Medicine (DGLRM) and the European Society of Aerospace Medicine Space Medicine Group (ESAM-SMG). Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med. 2020;28:108. doi:10.1186/s13049-020-00793-y

steps.text: Medication: per flight surgeon / onboard medical checklist.

source.guideline: team rule (Spec 5): medication stays with the flight surgeon; protocols never name a drug or dose

steps.text: The crewmember with the highest medical qualification decides whether to stop resuscitation, after consulting telemedicine support. If telemedicine is unavailable or the time delay prevents prompt feedback, they decide alone.

source.guideline: Hinkelbein J, et al. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) during spaceflight - a guideline for CPR in microgravity from the German Society of Aerospace Medicine (DGLRM) and the European Society of Aerospace Medicine Space Medicine Group (ESAM-SMG). Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med. 2020;28:108. doi:10.1186/s13049-020-00793-y
